answers.answer: Use printed Health and ignore Health modifiers.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. evidence.text: - **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. answers.answer: Yes. Powerstorm requires paying the repeated Power Card’s Energy cost again for each Repeat.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Yes. Powerstorm requires paying the repeated Power Card’s Energy cost again for each Repeat.
